clue.text: Providing loads of business that's awfully good

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
pious can mean excessively, sanctimoniously virtuous

explanation.surface: A firm whose output is plentiful is praised as wonderfully fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully good' reads as high praise, but here it means too good, holier-than-thou.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abundant supplies plenty, so it can be said to provide loads.

clue.text: Fish for tea, daily

definitions.meaning: British slang for a cup of tea
a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a charwoman

explanation.surface: A menu offers fish at teatime, every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row; 'daily' as a noun is the British term for a cleaning lady, also called a charlady.
explanation.definitionFit: All three senses share one spelling: a trout relative, slang for a cuppa, and a cleaning woman.

clue.text: Do well, having succeeded in right setting

indicators.note: a jewel's setting holds the stone, so the word for right is wrapped around the letter

parts.note: proper means right or correct
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone thrives after having triumphed in the correct environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' signals one piece placed within another, like a gem in its mount.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or thrive is to do well.

clue.text: Bouquet coming from so-called flower

indicators.note: so-called signals that the word is named aloud, sounding like the river's name

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Oder in central Europe

explanation.surface: A bunch of blooms gives off the scent of a particular flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river (it flows); the Oder sounds like the word for a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its smell or aroma.

clue.text: Namely one Celtic and rangers finally played?

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of rangers
played suggests the letters being worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Glasgow's two football clubs, Celtic and Rangers, have a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic and Rangers are Glasgow's rival football clubs. 'played' shuffles I, CELTIC and S (last of 'rangers').
explanation.definitionFit: Scilicet is a Latin term used in writing to introduce an explanation, meaning that is to say.

clue.text: Play about chap going back to Liverpool, say

indicators.note: going back means the man's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Sid is a typical man's name, a chap
Liverpool is an example of a port

explanation.surface: A man returns to Liverpool to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns SID into DIS; 'Play about' is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport is to frolic or amuse oneself, which is playing about.

clue.text: Mark time when one's powers decline

parts.note: a dot is a small mark
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Note the moment at which one's strength starts to wane.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is old age marked by weakening faculties, the period of decline.

clue.text: Nickname like this that in Paris Limey adopted

parts.note: so can mean in this way

indicators.note: adopted means the Briton takes in the French word

parts.note: Limey is American slang for a Briton
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A nickname of this sort is one a Briton picked up in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limey' is old American slang for a Briton, from the limes once issued to British sailors against scurvy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is an affectionate or descriptive name used instead of the real one.

clue.text: Protective coat of paint, sort not finished

parts.note: oils are oil paints

indicators.note: not finished means the word for sort loses its final letter

parts.note: kind means sort or type

explanation.surface: A sealing layer of paint comes out incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' belongs to the definition, though it seems to go with 'paint'. 'not finished' cuts KIND to KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof garment of oiled cloth, a coat that protects against rain.

clue.text: Versatile sportsman or woman? The latter I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether an all-rounder is a man or a woman, someone opts for the second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb of preference but is the anagram signal on THE LATTER I.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who swims, cycles and runs in one race must be an all-round athlete.

clue.text: Defender dropping point at end of a game

indicators.note: at end of places the word for point after the other pieces

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A defender lets a point slip at the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defender' suggests a footballer, but it means someone who argues in support of a cause; 'dropping' only sets the point down at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a doctrine or person, a champion of that cause.

clue.text: A lot of sea food from India?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe

explanation.surface: A lot of seafood is said to come from India.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits balti is a curry style popularised in Britain, from Pakistani cooking rather than Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: Balti is a kind of curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, served in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Repair kit kept with racing driver's fine?

indicators.note: to repair is to fix up, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A racing driver keeps a repair kit with him, which seems fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair kit' looks like a single item, but 'Repair' is the anagram signal on KIT KEPT plus RACING.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist who leaves a car in the wrong place is given a penalty notice.

clue.text: Clot swallowing speed with creep, one high on drugs

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for clot takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to clot is to set or thicken
pace means speed
a cad is a creep, a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A fool on amphetamines takes speed with a creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a noun for a fool and 'speed' like the drug, but they are a verb and a synonym of rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is a dreamy, spaced-out person, typically from drug use.

clue.text: Colourful singer's an old playboy favourite clothed

indicators.note: clothed means the favourite wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a rake is an old-fashioned word for a dissolute pleasure-seeker

explanation.surface: A bright vocalist is described as a former playboy, a well-dressed favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is a bird; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This small parrot has bright plumage and calls noisily, a bird with a vivid coat.

clue.text: Refuse to finish off drink quickly

definitions.meaning: to swallow a drink in one go

explanation.surface: Someone declines to down a drink in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Knock back means both to reject an offer and to gulp a drink down.

clue.text: Fish from top side of boat

definitions.meaning: a small eel-like sea fish, a butterfish
the upper edge of a boat's side, also spelt gunwale

explanation.surface: Fish are caught from the edge of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small eel-like fish and the upper rim of a hull, also spelt gunwale.

clue.text: Round lake, short boat race disturbed fish

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the letter for lake
disturbed means these letters are churned up into a new order
short means the word boat loses its final letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Near a lake, a curtailed boat race was upset by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims 'boat' to BOA; 'disturbed' shuffles BOA and RACE to ABACORE, and 'Round' puts that around L.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned tuna, a sea fish.

clue.text: Touched a bird

definitions.meaning: a grey European bird that lays its eggs in others' nests

explanation.surface: Someone tapped a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo means both crazy and the bird known for its two-note call.

clue.text: In battle, horse may be needed for battery

definitions.meaning: a war horse ridden by a cavalry officer
a device to restore the power of a rechargeable cell

explanation.surface: A horse in battle may be needed for an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' suggests an assault or artillery, keeping the military picture, but it is an electric cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a cavalry mount and also a device for recharging cells.

clue.text: Even pay with old copper

parts.note: flat means even or level
to foot a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: An old policeman's pay is the same as everyone's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is British slang for a police officer; flatfoot is dated slang for a beat cop.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatfoot is dated slang for a police officer who walks a beat.

clue.text: Soldiers secure old city

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to land something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Troops capture an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in Florida.

clue.text: Dull day extremely full of quarrels

indicators.note: full of means the outer letters hold the word for quarrels
extremely takes the first and last letters of day

parts.note: rows are quarrels

explanation.surface: A dreary day was packed with arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' looks like an adjective for the day, but it defines the answer, meaning sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sleepy makes one sluggish and heavy, so dull in that sense.

clue.text: Unsophisticated accompaniment to Christmas: lots of beer

parts.note: a cracker is a paper tube pulled at the Christmas dinner table in Britain
a barrel holds a large quantity of beer

explanation.surface: Christmas brings simple pleasures and plenty of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a British party novelty, a paper tube that bangs when pulled. Cracker-barrel describes homespun folksy wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracker-barrel means homespun and folksy, like talk around a country store's barrel.

clue.text: Way to conquer drug, initially

parts.note: to rout is to defeat decisively
E, the initial of ecstasy, stands for that drug

explanation.surface: A means to beat a drug habit, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: E is standard shorthand for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a path or road, a way to somewhere.

clue.text: Bullock upsetting little ones

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: A young bull is causing distress to small children.
explanation.definitionFit: Stot is a northern and Scottish word for a young castrated ox.

clue.text: Pointer perhaps to scholar's belief

parts.note: a pointer is a breed of gun dog
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A hint offered to an academic about his conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' is the hunting dog, not a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles held as true, a firm belief.

clue.text: I hunt down lost crime novel

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters are scattered and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader tracks down a missing detective story.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery story about solving a murder.

clue.text: Act essential for a jailer

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
key means essential

explanation.surface: Performing is vital for a prison guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for the warder holding a prison's keys.

clue.text: Make level university required during race, say

indicators.note: during means the university sits inside the event

parts.note: a race is an example of an event
OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning institution

explanation.surface: To even things out, a university was needed during the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To even out is to smooth or equalise, to make level.
